features.headline: How Vikings got Kirk Cousins ready to win on short notice
features.desc: Cousins and coach Kevin O'Connell deferred to each other until they each needed to take control Sunday.
body: EAGAN, Minn. — In their first season together with the Vikings in 2022, Kevin O'Connell and Kirk Cousins developed a decidedly polite Minnesotan relationship.

O'Connell, the head coach, worried about inadvertently insulting Cousins, his quarterback. In an interview with ESPN that season, Cousins recalled O'Connell telling him he was throwing the ball well in practice — but quickly adding that his praise did not mean he hadn't thrown well on other days.
Cousins, meanwhile, was super courteous about imposing on O'Connell's busy days as a first-time head coach, offensive playcaller and father of four — including a newborn daughter.
At times that season, Cousins waited for O'Connell to invite him into meetings before he would ask scheme questions or make game-plan suggestions.

That polite tap dance resumed last week when the two were reunited at the trade deadline, a personality mix that contributed heavily to the Vikings' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers. Cousins finished 21-of-31 for 207 yards, two touchdowns and an interception.
O'Connell said this week that he initially planned a light schematic burden because "I did not want him coming in here feeling like the weight of the world was on his shoulders in Week 1."
Cousins, meanwhile, acknowledged he worried about balancing his own ideas with overstepping his boundaries as a new player on the team.
"I've changed playcallers 11 times," Cousins said. "So it's this dance of when am I going to speak up and say, 'I'm not comfortable with that.

features.headline: The clock is ticking on Steph Curry's final act with the Warriors
features.desc: At 38, Curry is still brilliant — but managing his body has become the biggest battle of his career.
body: LATE LAST JANUARY, during an off-day workout in an empty downtown Minneapolis arena, Stephen Curry's right knee started bothering him.
Four days prior, he had been named an All-Star starter for an 11th time, averaging 27.2 points on extreme efficiency, keeping the Golden State Warriors' record at a respectable 25-21.
But his co-star, Jimmy Butler, had torn his right ACL the week before. Curry, at 37, was again dealing with overloaded schemes and an increased offensive burden. His knee started barking.
"That was the moment where I started to get concerned," Curry said. "It just didn't feel right."
Curry attempted to play through what he described as "a weird soreness and pain that didn't go away."

Despite being initially listed as questionable, he had 26 points against the Timberwolves, rested for a game and then scored 27 in Utah to close the road trip and 23 against the Detroit Pistons once the team returned home.
But neither the pain nor concern would subside.

"Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, 'Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'" Curry said. "And I was just faking it for the first whatever [25 minutes]."

There's something poetic about his final sequence before he left the game. Curry came off a third-quarter pindown into an isolation against Ausar Thompson and did what he described as "a high-step thing because it hurt so bad in that moment."

After the fidget, Curry shook Thompson with a crossover combination, hobbled into the lane and poured in an and-1 floater over one of the best perimeter defenders in the world to give him 23 points in those 25 minutes.

features.headline: MLB free agency tracker: 2026-27 offseason trades, moves
features.desc: We've got you covered on all the major MLB hot stove signings and trades.
body: The 2026-27 MLB hot stove was lit just days after the Milwaukee Brewers hoisted the franchise's first World Series championship trophy.

All eyes this winter are on the free agency of two-time Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal. But he's not the only one who will make a splash in the market, with Freddya Peralta, Randy Arozarena, Seiya Suzuki and Michael King among the other free agents to watch.
Which teams will go big to contend for the 2027 World Series title? And who will make the trades and signings that have everyone buzzing?
Below is a running list of notable transactions and updates from throughout the MLB offseason.
The Chicago White Sox are in agreement with free agent pitcher Dustin May on a three-year, $52.5 million deal, source confirms to ESPN.
Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan.
Reliever Ryan Walker went to the Milwaukee Brewers in a trade that sent right-handers Blake Holub and Gavin Perry to the San Francisco Giants.
First baseman Jake Bauers and the Boston Red Sox are in agreement on a four-year, $58 million contract, sources tell ESPN.
Reliever Evan Phillips and the Atlanta Braves are in agreement on a three-year, $35 million contract.
Jacob Young agreed to terms on a long-term contract with the Washington Nationals, president of baseball operations Paul Toboni announced.
Source: Detroit Tigers agree to one-year deal with reliever Emilio Pagan.
RHP Ryan Weiss agrees to $1.85M deal with San Diego Padres, sources say.

features.headline: Tarik Skubal free agency tracker: Latest on top MLB free agent
features.desc: Who will land the two-time Cy Young Award winner? We have all the latest updates on where things stand.
body: All eyes are on ace Tarik Skubal as MLB free agency gets underway ahead of the impending labor stoppage.

The current collective bargaining agreement expires on Dec. 1, meaning that after that, no players can sign until a new CBA is established. This could put Skubal on the fast track to a new contract, as many around the sport expect him to sign ahead of the lockout.
Where do things currently stand in Skubal's free agency? What's the latest? We have everything you need to know about the winter's No. 1 free agent in one place.
Skubal is scheduled to meet with the New York Mets in California next week, a source confirmed to ESPN on Tuesday.

While the Mets are an obvious possible landing spot for the two-time Cy Young Award winner, the other seemingly logical destination for Skubal is a return to the Los Angeles Dodgers, the team he was traded to from the Detroit Tigers at this year's deadline.

Nov. 11: Passan's perfect move for top contenders: Skubal has no interest in a shorter-term, higher-dollar deal, which could disadvantage the Dodgers. The Mets could be in the strongest position to land Skubal this offseason.

features.headline: Free agents to invest in, avoid during 2026-27 MLB offseason
features.desc: Here are this offseason's players to target and be wary of, given their projected contracts.
body: Now that we've projected contracts for the top 50 free agents in this winter's class, let's look at which players could provide the most — and least — bang for their expected buck.

In past years, I've done pretty well — investing in Sonny Gray, Shane Bieber and Shota Imanaga as free agents while avoiding the end of Justin Turner's career and megadeals for players whom teams initially didn't sign to long-term contracts that offseason, like Blake Snell, Pete Alonso, and Cody Bellinger, before they all eventually got those deals.

Last year, my biggest player to invest in was a hit (Michael King), and my five players to avoid combined for -0.3 WAR at over $62 million in salary and over $40 million in future commitments. Now, I'm back again to try to hit the bull's-eye a few more times.

The projected contracts in my rankings provide important context for this exercise, as my choices are based on return on investment — how I expect the players to perform over the length of their deals at their projected prices.

The rules for this edition are the same I set out for myself last winter: Each group of three players must have one player projected to land more than $50 million, one projected for a one-year deal and at least one pitcher and one position player.

features.headline: Breaking down the major futures for the Big Ten, from the Heisman to the CFP
features.desc: Let's evaluate whether a standout performance on a three-loss team and a 10-0 team are real or a mirage in the Big Ten.
body: There are only two weeks left in the college football regular season, and there are not many chances left to make some noise. The Heisman race still has room for a late push, but I'm ready to pick my winner, even if his team ends up missing the playoff.

Meanwhile in California, unbeaten UCLA has gone from a great story to a team we need to take seriously. But just how seriously? That depends on which trophy we're talking about, and what price we're getting.

Let's dive into the Heisman odds and why I'm ready to make my call for a Big Ten star, then take a look at how UCLA compares to its potential opponent in the conference championship game — and whether it says more about the Bruins or the Big Ten.
I'm ready to call it. Jeremiah Smith is winning the Heisman. Ohio State has lost three games, but Smith hasn't stopped showing up, with 164 yards at Texas and 133 yards against Oregon.
He has 80 catches, 1,317 yards and 15 touchdowns with production against good teams, not just the easy ones. I'm not making him pay for everything wrong with Ohio State.
He's my winner, but picking him and laying -144 with games still left are two different decisions. I'm not buying now, but hopefully you have an early-season ticket on him by reading this column.

Mensah is the reason Smith isn't a lock, having completed 76.3% of his passes with 29 touchdowns against two interceptions. And even without WR Malachi Toney, he just threw for 382 yards against Duke.

He can keep this offense moving without his biggest playmaker. If he finishes strong and Miami wins the ACC, he gives voters a real alternative to Smith. He's my biggest threat, even if I'm still picking the receiver to win.
